name: close the workspace's context leaks, measured against live adopters
objective: Measure where the workspace actually spends context across four live adopting repos (changple5 v36, changple_web v35, Mijual v36, arb_upbit_1 v35 -- ~1,140 slices, 83 archived phases between three of them), then close only the leaks the measurement justifies. Confirmed leak with an operator-proposed remedy to research first: per-review durable-doc consolidation rewrites whole docs that only grow (changple5 backend.md at v0054, 420 KB, rewritten by every review) -- research retiring doc-new-version from the review slice in favour of dedicated operator-created docs phases, and what a review still records if so. Open questions: whether the 16 KB phase.md budget is right (post-v35 notebooks ride within bytes of the ceiling -- is mid-phase compaction losing decisions under that pressure?); whether plan.md + result.md suffice as the orchestrator's post-slice record; what the review may read instead of every result.md; executor validation cost; where keep-tests-small needs teeth (changple5: 494 test files / 6.3 MB; the other three comply). Two suspects retracted by measurement: archiving works (rotate-backlog; 56/20/7 archived) and the notebook budget is respected since v35. DECOMP cuts a research slice first -- the fix list is not knowable before the measurement -- and DECOMP2 cuts the remedies from findings. Machinery and doctrine only: adopter repos are read as evidence and receive a documented procedure, never edits from here.

review.note: Objective met; doc-rewrite leak closed by generalising the v24 parallel deferred path (v38); all slices re-validated together, v38 lifecycle probed end-to-end in scratch; one dropped decision restored in-review; OQ1/OQ3/OQ4 filed as D14-D16, OQ2 refreshed on D8

acceptance.note: machinery and doctrine only; no operator-visible running product
